metadata.title: What Could Push Broadcom Stock Higher Is Already Sitting In Its Order Book

content.text:
Broadcom's handful of core customers are now ordering compute far ahead of delivery because power and memory set the pace, which hands the company a forward view semiconductor companies rarely get.
The Order Book Grew A Year Longer In One Quarter
Broadcom (AVGO) took in more than $30 billion of AI semiconductor orders in fiscal Q2 2026 against the $10.8 billion it shipped. The shipped figure set a record; the booked one matters more, because by the company's own account its order visibility now runs to 2028. In March 2026 it ran only to 2027.
Its Customers Are Ordering Compute They Cannot Plug In Yet
That gap is not a demand burst. Management says those orders are not for near-term delivery: Broadcom's six core AI customers must line up electrical power, high-bandwidth memory and wafer supply before a chip is any use to them, so they commit well ahead of delivery. A business normally sold quarter to quarter now carries something closer to a contract book, with AI chip revenue alone guided above $100 billion in fiscal 2027, more than the $75.5 billion of total revenue the company recorded over the trailing twelve months.
The Networking Cushion Is Expected To Get Thinner
The catch comes from management itself. The custom accelerators driving that book carry lower margins than much of the rest of its semiconductor line, while the AI networking shipped alongside them carries rich ones that partly offset the pressure. Customers stay with that networking: Broadcom's SerDes let them run chip-to-chip links over direct attach copper. But networking was almost 40% of fiscal Q2 2026 AI revenue, and management expects that share to settle nearer 30%, so the offset gets proportionally smaller exactly as the lower-margin revenue scales.
The Upside Is Real, And Operating Margin Is The Test
The upside case is still real, and better evidenced than most. There is precedent for a fast move: Broadcom stock has gained more than 30% inside two months on 17 occasions since 2010, five of those past 50%, and it sits about 18% below its 52-week high. The number that settles the case is operating margin, guided to hold near 67% in fiscal Q3 2026 even as consolidated gross margin steps down about three points on the revenue mix between semiconductors and software. Those results are now due. If operating leverage absorbs that pressure, that forward book converts into earnings; if it does not, that revenue is worth less than it looks. The other thing to watch is concentration, since management concedes a core custom-silicon customer will spread its sourcing. For companies actually raising their own bar, our screen of stocks whose guidance keeps climbing is where to start.
